Grid Systems in Graphic Design

Josef Müller-Brockmann’s manual of the grid, with the grid itself drawn on its cover.

Source
eMuseum, Museum für Gestaltung Zürich: A JMBR 181-1-6
Creator
Josef Müller-Brockmann
Made
1981
Style
International Typographic Style (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Systematic, didactic, rational, clear
Evidence
Downloaded the cover scan File:Raster-Systeme-Cover.jpg (1200 × 1663 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. Interior pages were not seen. The image is not stored.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Rastersysteme für die visuelle Gestaltung / Grid systems in graphic design, 1981; bilingual German and English, subtitled a handbook for graphic designers, typographers, and exhibition designers. The eMuseum holds the cover and several cover drafts from the Müller-Brockmann archive, donated by Shizuko Yoshikawa. eMuseum object 167597.

Wikipedia’s bibliography lists it as published by Arthur Niggli, Niederteufen, 1981, ISBN 9783721201451. Wikipedia: Josef Müller-Brockmann.

Müller-Brockmann was a founding editor of Neue Grafik and designed Der Film.

Observed

  • The cover is a flat orange with a grid of thin white lines: four columns and several rows separated by narrow gutters.
  • Black grotesque type sits exactly on the grid. The two titles, “Grid systems” and “Raster systeme”, are the largest elements and start at the left margin.
  • Subtitles and the author’s name are small and flush left, starting either at the left margin or at the third column line.
  • The publisher’s name “Niggli” sits alone near the bottom, on the same column line as the author’s name.
  • Only three colors appear: orange, black, and white.

Why it belongs

Showing the grid lines on the cover makes the invisible structure of the style visible, and turns a method into an image.

Borrow

Start text blocks on only two or three column lines, and repeat those lines throughout the layout.

Consider revealing the grid as thin lines when the subject is structure or documentation.

Use one saturated flat background color with black type and white rules.
